newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent trims losses, brokers leery of reversal.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent trims losses, brokers leery of reversal.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures trimmed their losses by midsession as brokers said they braced for a possible reversal in prices after Tuesday's sharp selloff may have factored in the bearish U.S. inventory data.

But they waited for confirmation of American Petroleum Institute data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration, especially after the two reports last week painted opposite changes in gasoline inventories.
At 1100 GMT, July Brent was 10 cents lower at $18.80 a barrel, recovering from a session low of $18.73 to hit a peak of $18.87.
June gas oil was $2 lower at $168 a tonne, trapped in a $1 range.

"It's important to watch in the first hour how the U.S. reacts," said Charles Gray, energy analyst at Prudential Bache Futures. "If it fails to follow through (on the downside) then people may say the data was built into the price."
June gas oil was seen facing resistance at an upside gap from $168.50 to $169.75 and support at an uptrend line crossing near today' low of $167.50.
July Brent has its own tiny gap from $18.87 to $18.88.
"With hindsight it seems that some participants had early information about the API stats which were clearly bearish," said Leslie Nicholas, energy analyst at GNI Ltd.

"However, much of the downside work attributable purely to the stats was priced in yesterday and bearing in mind the suspicion the market possesses towards recent API data, the DOE figures will be watched closely later today," he said.
"Overall short term fundamentals have clearly taken a turn for the worse but we will have to see what happens to refining margins over the next few days."
